title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Unknown/Reserved Error Code Handling Architecture
purpose: Define DoQ adapter behavior for STOP_SENDING server-side dispatch prevention, unsolicited RESET_STREAM client-side tolerance, and registered error code pathway documentation.
design_summary: Three independent enhancements: (1) DoqServer.HandleQueryStreamAsync now checks for STOP_SENDING after reading the query but before dispatching to the DNS handler, preventing processing when the client has cancelled. (2) DoqClient adds a configurable MaxUnsolicitedResets property that tolerates a set number of unsolicited RESET_STREAM frames from the server before closing the connection. (3) DoqErrorCode documents the registered-specific-code pathway per RFC 9250 section 8.4, supported by the existing NormalizeReceivedErrorCode helper.
data_and_state_considerations: The server adds no new state. The client adds an atomic reset counter and a configurable threshold.
edge_cases_and_constraints: MaxUnsolicitedResets of 0 (default) preserves backward-compatible immediate connection close on any RESET_STREAM.
The STOP_SENDING check is a lightweight task-completed probe that completes synchronously when no abort is pending.
The registered-specific-code pathway is documented but not enforced; the existing NormalizeReceivedErrorCode continues to map unknown codes.
risks: STOP_SENDING received exactly between the read completing and the dispatch check is a narrow race that is addressed by the post-read probe.
Unsolicited RESET_STREAM counting is shared across all queries on the same connection; a high rate of resets across different queries can exhaust the budget.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: All changes are confined to the DoQ adapter layer. No QUIC transport modifications are required. The STOP_SENDING dispatch check uses the existing WriteAbortTask pattern; the RESET_STREAM tolerance uses a simple atomic counter.
